chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Muhammad from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, all from al-Wasshash, from Ahmad ibn A'idh, from Abi Khadija, from Mu'la ibn Khunays, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man said to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), 'O Messenger of Allah, teach me.' He said, 'Go and do not be angry.' The man said, 'I am content with that,' and went to his people. He found that a conflict had arisen among them; they had lined up in rows and put on their weapons. When he saw that, he put on his weapon, then stood with them. Then he remembered the words of the Messenger of Allah, 'Do not be angry,' so he threw down the weapon and came walking to the people who were the enemies of his people, saying, 'O you all! Whatever injury, or killing, or a blow without lasting effect was from you, upon me is (the compensation) from my wealth; I will fulfill it for you.' The people said, 'So whatever it was, it is for you; we are more entitled to it than you are.' He said, 'So the people reconciled and the anger departed.'
He said, 'So the people reconciled and the anger departed.'
ai.seo_question: What is the concise advice the Prophet gave for controlling anger and resolving conflict?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated in al-Kafi, highlights the Prophet’s (peace be upon him and his family) concise advice of 'Do not be angry' as a comprehensive key to success, a concept often linked to the famous narration of Imam Ali (peace be upon him). The narrative illustrates the practical application of this virtue in tribal warfare, where self-restraint and financial compensation for minor injuries effectively neutralize hostility and secure peace. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that mastering anger is not merely emotional control but a strategic tool for social harmony and conflict resolution.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, and Ali Bin Muhammad, from Salih Bin Abu Hammad, altogether from Al Washha, from Ahmad Bin A’iz, from Abu Khadeeja, from Moalla Bin Khunays, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘A man said to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! Teach me (something)’. He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Go and don’t be angry’. So the man said, ‘I have suffice with that’. So he went to his family and he found that there was a battle in between his people, and they had lined up in rows and wearing the weapons.
So when he saw that, he (also) wore his weapon, then stood along with them. Then he remembered the words of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, ‘Don’t be angry’. So he threw down the weapon, then went walking over to the people who were the enemies of his people, and he said, ‘O you all! Whatever injuries were with you, or (if) a killing, or a strike in which there were no effects, so upon me is (the compensation for it) from my wealth. I shall fulfil it’. So the people said, ‘So whatever it was, so it is for you, (although) we are first for it with that than you are (i.e. we don’t want anything)’.
He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘So the people reconciled and the hostility was gone’.
en.sarwar: 11. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu’alla ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Muhammad from Salih ibn abu Hammad all from al-Washsha’ from Ahmad ibn ‘A’id from abu Khadijah from Mu’alla ibn Khanis from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

Once a man said to the Holy Prophet, ‘O Messenger of Allah, teach me.’ The Messenger of Allah said, ‘You may go and do not become angry.’ The man said, ‘I have taken it as a sufficient lesson.’ He went to his family and found his people fighting, all of them lined up in arms. When he saw it he also armed himself and stood up in line with them and then he remembered the words of the Messenger of Allah, ‘Do not become angry’. He threw away his arms and moved forward to the enemies of his people and said, ‘O people, I will take responsibility for any loss of life, serious or slight injury that you may have suffered, I will pay you.’ The people said, ‘Whatever happened we give permission to go in your favor. It is more proper for us to make such undertakings.’
The Imam then said, ‘The people made peace and anger was gone.’”
